text:
Good evening! It's a September-feeling Wednesday in early November, with sunshine and a high near 72, and the sun sets at 4:37 under mostly clear skies. Enjoy it, because the warmth won't last long.

Clouds fill in after dark, and a gusty south wind picks up, 8 to 17 mph with gusts up to 29. That keeps tonight very mild, with a low around 58, which is more like a typical early October afternoon.

Thursday starts dry for a few minutes, then showers move in around 7 or 8am. The best chance for steady rain is 9am to noon, and then it eases up. Amounts are light, about a tenth of an inch, though the European model is wetter than the rest, so a few heavier downpours are possible. A second round could brush us around 6 or 7pm, ending before 11. Expect a high near 67 and a breezy day, with gusts near 29 again.

Grab the umbrella and a light jacket for the morning commute. Friday looks mostly dry, with temperatures in the low 60s, and then it turns cooler for the weekend.

KEY MESSAGE 1: GOES-19 mid lvl water vapor imagery indicates ridge and subsidence is directly overhead this aftn while ribbons of better mid lvl moisture is angling toward the SLV/western NY. Meanwhile, deep and closed off vertically stacked cyclonic circulation is over the northern Plains with strong southerly warm-moist conveyor belt acrs the Ohio Valley. This deep moisture advection, combined with initial pre-trof 700-500mb s/w energy wl result in a broken line of showers on Thurs. Crnt proggs have highest probability of precip btwn 12z-18z, with secondary line of precip possible btwn 21z-00z. Did note a weak sliver of MUCAPE of 150-300 J/kg, so a rumble or two of thunder is possible. However, given the weak thermodynamics and forcing confidence is low on thunder, so have not mention in grids attm. Rainfall amounts wl vary from one to location to another, given the scattered nature of showers, but with pw values 1.25 to 1.40" a few heavier downpours are possible. Basin average rainfall mainly btwn 0.10 and 0.25" with highest values over the High Peaks in Essex County, NY. A very warm night is anticipated tonight with lows mid 40s to near 60F, due to increasing clouds and southerly flow. Coolest values deeper protected valleys of central/eastern VT and warmest CPV. As gradient strengthens btwn approaching cold front and departing ridge the 925mb to 850mb wind fields increase btwn 25 and 45 knots tonight into Thurs. The latest RRFS sounding profiles at BTV and CLCR show 300 feet agl winds of 25 to 35 knots, but warmer air moving over cooler warm suggests a stable bl. Still believe with 33 knots at 300 feet agl a Lake Wind Advisory wl be required tonight into Thursday. KEY MESSAGE 2: Latest synoptic scale progs show additional deepening of mid/upper lvl cyclonic circulation over the central Great Lakes, while elongated vorticity and associated sfc boundary is draped acrs the eastern seaboard. The system looks just a little unphased on Friday with our cwa underneath mid lvl dry slot. This should result in a mostly dry Friday with comfortable temps well into the 60s. As closed circulation moves toward western NY/PA weak low pres develops over SNE coast with invert trof extending back toward central NY. This complex mid/upper system and associated track of sfc low pres and placement/amount of precip on Friday night into Saturday is still to be determined. The highest probabilities from the NBM are acrs central/eastern VT attm, but would not be surprised if chances expand back toward northern NY, given the closed circulation. As system evolves on Saturday, expect developing cyclonic upslope flow to occur, placing highest pops/qpf acrs the northern Dacks into the central/northern Greens. Still some uncertainty on timing of upslope flow and when the cooler air aloft arrives. Temps wl be slowly stepping back toward normal by this upcoming weekend. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Wednesday! Wednesday could start with a bit of leftover cloud cover, but we get more sunshine going through the day. With that sun, it’ll feel a lot more like September than early November as sunshine sends our temperatures soaring into the low and mid-70s. This will be warm enough to break or tie records all across the area. Clouds start to fill back in by Wednesday night, as lows fall back into the 50s. Thursday morning looks to start dry for most, before showers begin to roll through from west to east in the mid to late morning hours. Right now, it looks like we all see rain, but it’s not a ton with most only running a couple tenths of an inch of new rain. Temperatures are a tad cooler with most in the low to mid-60s. Friday looks drier, but there could still be a spotty shower here and there. We continue to lose a little bit of ground temperature wise, as most talk high temperatures in the upper 50s and lower 60s. The weekend could again feature a few showers for Saturday. Temperatures turn noticeably cooler with most only in the 40s to about 50 for Saturday afternoon. Sunday looks drier, but again could feature a spotty morning shower or two. Temperatures are generally stuck in the 40s for most.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-03T22:30:00Z — same caveat): Sun and record warmth for some Wednesday — Wednesday turns much warmer, as highs reach the low to mid-70s region-wide. A couple towns may approach 80! Some towns likely set a new daily record high. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with a noticeable south breeze. Thursday stays mild, with highs in the mid-60s. An approaching cold front brings a mostly cloudy sky and scattered showers. A late evening thunderstorm cannot be ruled out in southern Vermont. The south breeze becomes a bit stronger, with gusts near 30. Friday turns drier, with only a spot shower leftover. A few hours of sunshine are likely, before clouds thicken up through the afternoon. Highs again reach the 60s. This weekend turns much cooler, an an upper-level low sends highs back closer to 50. Expect lots of clouds with a few additional showers, especially on Saturday.
